OWNER SPECIFICATION REVIEW EVENT, r11 Part A (the ten-row owner packet), 2026-09-16.
Recorded under the r11 closure mandate's AFK review authority on an explicit owner ruling,
transcribed verbatim in work/r11-campaign/RULINGS-OWNER-10.md. This is a CLAIM CORRECTION:
the registry is brought to what the code already does, and no implementation was weakened.

RULING (row 4): ACCEPT the replacement. Scope-only; `statement` and `security_consequence`
are unchanged.

SOURCE: not an R11 row. Surfaced by fixing R11-598 / R11-370.

WHAT MOVED: one paragraph of `scope`. It disclaimed "an arbitrary `ResolvesServerCert`
supplied to `TlsListenerSecurityState::build_delegated_resolver_config`" and said "That
escape hatch exists for custody arrangements MCP-RE does not model".

WHY THAT WAS WRONG, descriptively. `build_delegated_resolver_config` became PRIVATE in
a50d4070 (#886, closing R11-594). Its only caller is `build_delegated_config`, which goes
through `validated_delegated_resolver` -> `DelegatedCertResolver::materialize` — the
correspondence gate, with the listener's own budget. The paragraph disclaimed a route that no
longer exists, so it was vacuous; worse, it told a reader an unsupported public route into
delegated serving is available, which is the opposite of true. The R11-594 adjudication
flagged this prose as needing a re-read once the second half was fixed.

THE CORRECTED SCOPE says positively that within the API this crate publishes,
delegated-resolver materialization has no route that bypasses the validated correspondence
gate — `build_delegated_resolver_config` is private and its one caller goes through
`materialize`, and the handshake signing key's constructor is reachable only inside
`crate::delegated_tls`. It then keeps the true boundary explicitly outside the claim: that is
a fact about what this crate PUBLISHES, not unconstructibility, because
`rustls::sign::SigningKey` and `RawEd25519TlsSigner` are public traits and an embedder
writing its own resolver is outside this claim exactly as before.

WHY THE OLD TEXT WAS NOT MERELY HARMLESS. "The escape hatch exists for custody arrangements
MCP-RE does not model" is the kind of sentence a future author reads as permission to reopen
one. Historical permission text is not preserved because a hatch used to exist.
